Step 2 · A fake is born

Same samples, different continuous waves

Record one point every Δt=1/fₛ seconds. Different continuous waves can produce exactly the same samples: aliasing. Initially f=9 Hz and fₛ=10 Hz; the pink curve uses signed frequency g=−1 Hz and still passes through every gold sample. The sign means sin(2πgt)=−sin(2π|g|t), not a negative frequency magnitude. Select sample n, then change f or fₛ. The circled sample time and diamond-marked non-sample time are checked against the SAME curves below. Aliasing generally begins above fₛ/2; fₛ need not fall below f.

Signal frequency f (Hz) 9
Sample rate f_s (Hz) 10

Gold circle: actual sample n. Cyan dashed line and open diamonds: t=(n+¼)/fₛ BETWEEN samples, a comparison only, not an extra sample. Original is grey; folded is pink. Diamonds can coincide.

Select integer sample n (arrows ±1)

Current n = 1

Reset this step
Classic slow wave: f=9, f_s=10
Pinned to one phase: f=f_s=10
Folded: f=14, f_s=20
No aliasing: f=3, f_s=25

g = f − k·fs; falias = |g|

This page uses k=round(f/fₛ), placing signed g=f−k·fₛ in [−fₛ/2,fₛ/2], then takes the frequency magnitude |g|. Endpoints have representation ambiguity: see Step 3. Draw with g, not |g| in an unchanged-phase sine. Other steps retain the same folding function.

f = 9.0 Hz · fₛ = 10.0 Hz · k = 1 · g = −1 Hz · f_alias = |g| = 1.0 Hz — that is the fake wave

Spacing Δt≈0.1 s; n=1, tₙ≈0.1 s: original≈−0.5877853, folded≈−0.5877853, difference≈-2.22e-16. Equal in theory; displayed arithmetic includes floating-point roundoff.

NON-sample comparison t≈0.125 s: original≈0.7071068, folded≈−0.7071068, difference≈1.414214. Values use unit amplitude. They may differ here, or happen to agree.

Why equal samples? At tₙ=n/fₛ the phase difference is 2π(f−g)n/fₛ=2πkn: an integer number of turns. Sine returns to the same value after every whole turn. Thus sin(2πftₙ)=sin(2πgtₙ) for every integer n. Away from sample times, that whole-turn condition is no longer guaranteed.

This compares two ideal zero-initial-phase, unit-amplitude sine candidates. A few coincident points do not identify an arbitrary continuous signal. Even when these curves coincide, higher aliases remain possible. Unique reconstruction needs a known bandlimit, the complete ideal uniform sample sequence and the corresponding reconstruction conditions; neither straight joins nor this finite plot prove it.

With default9/10, predict equal values at the circle and possibly different values at the diamonds, then move n to check. Why do both displayed curves coincide at3/25? k=0 and g=f; higher candidates such as28 Hz still share the samples.

The nastiest preset is “pinned to one phase”: when f is an exact multiple of fs, every peek lands on exactly the same phase, all dots collapse to a single value — no matter how fast the wave, it looks frozen. That is the truth behind the “stopped” wheel in step 0.

text:
第 2 步 · 混叠诞生

相同采样点，也能属于另一条波

在原波上每隔 Δt=1/fₛ 秒取一个点，不同连续波可能给出完全相同的点，这叫混叠。默认原波 f=9 Hz、采样率 fₛ=10 Hz，粉红曲线采用带符号频率 g=−1 Hz，仍逐点穿过金色样点。负号表示 sin(2πgt)=−sin(2π|g|t)，不是负的频率大小。选一个样点 n，再改 f 或 fₛ：圈出的采样时刻与菱形标出的非采样时刻，都用下面同一模型对账。别名通常在 f 超过 fₛ/2 时发生，不必等到 fₛ 小于 f。

信号频率 f（Hz） 5
采样率 f_s（Hz） 10

金色圆圈：第 n 个真实样点。青色虚线与空心菱形：两次采样之间的 t=(n+¼)/fₛ，仅作比较，不是额外样本。原波灰色，折叠波粉红；菱形可能重合。

选择整数样点 n（方向键 ±1）

当前 n = 1

重置本步
经典慢波：f=9, f_s=10
全钉同一点：f=f_s=10
折叠：f=14, f_s=20
无混叠：f=3, f_s=25
